name: Human Imperfection Pattern Interrupt
use_when: A truthful interruption, laugh, small mistake, or unscripted interaction makes the creator or subject feel more human.
The edit has become too polished, predictable, or emotionally distant.
A short-form story needs connection before returning to the main promise.
avoid_when: The moment creates consent, privacy, safety, brand, or dignity risk.
The interruption distracts from the main story without adding connection.
The deliverable requires formal polish, legal precision, or a cinematic style with no creator-human texture.

timeline_pattern.connection_rule: Keep the imperfection only when it reveals warmth, surprise, humor, vulnerability, or character.
timeline_pattern.reset_rule: After the interrupt, use a clean cut, breath, ambience, or brief drop to signal return to the main story.
timeline_pattern.truth_rule: Do not stage a fake imperfection and present it as spontaneous documentary truth.

motion.rule: Crop, punch in, or gently zoom toward the reaction only if it helps the viewer read the human beat.

keyframe_values.reaction_push: Use a subtle 105-115% push when a face or reaction needs focus.
keyframe_values.hold_time: Hold until the reaction is readable; in fast shorts, trim the exit as soon as the connection beat lands.

sound.rule: Preserve natural voice, laugh, room tone, or tiny movement sound when it makes the moment feel real.
sound.avoid: Do not bury the human moment under meme SFX unless the format is intentionally comedic.

captions.rule: Caption only the words needed for comprehension; nonverbal warmth often works better without extra text.
captions.avoid: Do not place captions over the face or reaction that carries the interrupt.

color.rule: Keep the human beat visually compatible with the surrounding edit; do not over-style it until it feels fake.

implementation.ffmpeg: Cut the interrupt as its own segment, preserve or smooth room tone with short fades, and test alternate exits around the reset point.
implementation.remotion: Represent the interrupt as a patternInterrupt sequence with reason, consentRisk, holdFrames, and resetFrame fields.
implementation.blender: Use only restrained camera motion if recreating the beat; the performance should remain primary.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Keep the unscripted clip, trim the entry/exit tightly, and use minimal captions/effects.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Duplicate the sequence and A/B a clean removal versus a human-interrupt version; choose the version with stronger connection and no risk.

common_mistakes: Cutting out the most relatable moment because it is not technically perfect.
Keeping every mistake instead of only the ones that add connection.
Letting an interrupt run past the moment where it stops adding value.
Adding heavy effects that make the human beat feel staged.
Ignoring consent, privacy, or dignity concerns around bystanders.
qc: Can the editor name the connection value of the imperfection?
Does the interrupt return to the main story before momentum dies?
Is any consent, privacy, safety, or brand risk resolved?
Do captions, zooms, or SFX avoid covering the human reaction?
Would the edit feel colder or less trustworthy if the moment were removed?
